name: Avici Card
summary: Avici is a Solana-based crypto card built around self-custody: your funds stay in your wallet until the moment you pay, and a collateral-based credit model lets you keep your crypto exposure. It targets DeFi-native users with Visa Signature acceptance, 5% cashback and gas-sponsored transactions.

kyc.notes: Avici requires identity verification before issuing a card, but does not ask for proof of address or a selfie at this tier.

pros: True self-custody — funds stay in your wallet until purchase
No monthly fees, top-up fees or maintenance charges
Visa Signature accepted at 90+ million merchants
Supports Apple Pay and Google Pay contactless payments
Gas-sponsored transactions on Solana and Base
cons: Collateral-based system carries liquidation risk if crypto drops
FX fees can reach up to 3% on international transactions
Not available in India, China, Russia or sanctioned countries
Newer platform with an evolving fee structure

faq.question: What is the Avici card?
faq.answer: Avici is a Solana-based crypto card that combines self-custody with a collateral-based credit model. Your funds stay in your wallet until you spend, and you can borrow against your crypto instead of selling it.

faq.question: Does Avici require KYC?
faq.answer: Yes. Avici requires identity verification (ID document) before issuing a card. Proof of address and a selfie are not requested at this tier.

faq.question: Where is the Avici card not available?
faq.answer: Avici is not available in India, China, Russia or sanctioned countries. Availability can change, so confirm your region in the app before applying.

faq.question: What fees does the Avici card charge?
faq.answer: Avici has no monthly, issuance or top-up fees. It charges around 1% FX on non-USD spending (up to 3% in some cases) and ATM withdrawals cost US$1 plus 0.65%.
